source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: Comitatives are formed with the same suffix as reciprocals from transitive as well as intransitive bases. They do not change the argument structure of the underlying predicate nor do they reduce case. What they seem to do is to introduce semantically an additional argument which can be optionally expressed by a noun phrase in the comitative case or by a postpositional phrase Lena-ny kytta ‘with Lena (Lena-acc with)’. If the additional argument is not expressed overtly, its presence is obligatorily implied. Note that a comitative DP can also be inserted in non-comitative (74) but it will not have an argument status as evidenced by the above contrast in (62/63). Commitative.
en: Michil is building a house together with someone else.
